summary.name: Screenshots
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source (MIT) macOS menu bar app for screenshots, scrolling capture, text copy via OCR, annotation, pinning, and screen recording to MP4 or GIF, with no cloud or network features.
use_cases: capture a full scrolling web page into one image
blur emails or values before sharing
record the screen as a GIF or video
keep a reference image floating above other windows
summary.what_it_does: The app lives in the macOS menu bar and is triggered by keyboard shortcuts (⌥⇧⌘ plus a number). After a capture it is copied to the clipboard, saved to the Desktop, and shown as a card for dragging into other apps. Annotation tools include arrows, shapes, text, pencil, highlighter, numbering, blur, and spotlight dimming. It can scroll and stitch a page into one image, copy text from an image using Apple's Vision framework, pin captures above other windows, and record the screen to video or GIF. A local history keeps a copy of each capture for a chosen retention period.
notable: Open-source under MIT license, source on GitHub
Text recognition runs locally with Apple's Vision framework
No cloud, share links, accounts or telemetry
Signed and notarized by Apple; installable via curl script or .dmg
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14 or newer
Microphone audio recording requires macOS 15 or newer
No dark mode, video trimming, or camera recording yet
Scrolling auto-scroll needs Accessibility permission; screen capture needs Screen Recording permission
